_comment: Harness-relevant Prometheus series, kept in ONE place so a metric rename
on the rate-control branch is a one-line change here, not a code edit
(harness plan, open question 7).
The scraper keeps a scraped series when its name STARTS WITH one of the
base names below. Prefix matching absorbs any suffix the OpenTelemetry ->
Prometheus exporter appends (e.g. `_total`, a unit suffix such as
`_milliseconds`), so the base name written here matches whether or not the
exporter renames it. Verify the exact scraped names and the `origin` label
value against a live /metrics scrape before trusting a run: run
`./run_ratecontrol.sh --probe <scenario>` (or curl the endpoint) and
confirm the names and the origin label appear as expected. Discovered
names are written to `discovered_metrics.txt` in every run directory.
Names verified against a live scrape of spiced
v2.4.0-unstable-build.41116b5ae9 (branch 14575-cluster-adaptive-rate-control,
built with --features rate-control) on 2026-10-01. The adaptive group used
to name `..._adaptive_rate_control_effective_limit` and
`..._admission_coefficient_permille`; neither exists in the runtime. What
ships is one f64 gauge in [0, 1] (`adaptive_admission_ratio`) and a
throttle counter, so the permille conversion is gone too.
The `cluster` group is present only when
`runtime.source_rate_control.state_location` is set; those series carry a
`limiter` label as well as `origin`, and the scraper keeps only `origin`,
so a dataset configured with more than one rate limit (both a per-second
and a per-minute limit) would emit two rows per scrape that this scraper
cannot tell apart.
